# Route audit: can a person reach it, and is it good (7 October 2026)

Handoff D.2. Every page under `apps/web/src/app` outside `(dev)` and `/preview`:
**224 pages** (the handoff said about 223). Generated by
`scripts/audit/route-reach.mjs`, which is committed so this can be re-run:

```
node scripts/audit/route-reach.mjs          # counts and lists per class
node scripts/audit/route-reach.mjs --md     # the table below
node scripts/audit/route-reach.mjs --nav <copy of nav-model.ts>   # try a different side navigation
```

## How reach is computed, not guessed

A page's surface is its `page.tsx`, every `layout.tsx` and `template.tsx` above it,
and everything those import, followed transitively. A link is a path written where
the product sends somebody: `href=`, `href:`, `router.push/replace`, `redirect(`,
`NextResponse.redirect`, `location.assign`, `new URL("/x"`, route constants
(`PROMOTION_HUB_HREF`), and template literals with an interpolated id (how a list
reaches its `[id]` child). Notification hrefs the database writes (in
`supabase/migrations`) count as taps from `/notifications`. Files that name routes
without sending anybody (`lib/nav/*`, sitemap, robots, the proxy, tests, the
first-run table, the desks' keyboard shortcuts) are not linkers. Then a
breadth-first walk from the side navigation, the dock and the landing page.

| Class | Meaning | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NAV | A row in `nav-model.ts` or a tab on the dock | 24 |
| ONE_TAP | Linked from the surface of a NAV destination (includes the shell every signed-in page wears) | 128 |
| DEEPER | Two or more taps from the nav, the dock or the landing page | 13 |
| DYN_CHILD | A dynamic route (`[id]`) reached from a reachable list | 50 |
| EXTERNAL | Not in the graph, but an email, SMS, share link or the service worker sends people there | 4 |
| ORPHAN | Only by typing the address | 5 |

With the lead's working copy of `nav-model.ts` (Receipts, Payouts and Refunds added
as Money rows) NAV is 27 and ONE_TAP 125; nothing else moves.

**The headline.** Almost nothing is unreachable any more. The problem section 3.1
describes is not orphans, it is depth: the money surfaces (`/receipts`, `/refunds`,
`/payouts`) are one tap inside `/payments` or `/settings`, which is reachable but is
not where somebody opening the side navigation looks. ONE-PRODUCT-DECISIONS.md puts
all three in the Money group; until the nav rows land they read as missing.

No side-nav row. |
| `/settings/invite/referrals/[id]` | A placeholder detail page (empty state only). Its list `/settings/invite/referrals` is itself an honest "not shown here" placeholder, while `/rewards/referrals` draws the real list. | Retire both settings pages into `/rewards/referrals` (Money group, Rewards row). Left alone here because `invite-honesty.test.ts` encodes the current contract; the lead should decide. |
| `/styleguide` | Internal design reference, `noindex`. | Deliberately unlinked from the product. If staff want it, a row on `/admin/reference`. |
| `/host/start`, `/sign-in/email` | Redirect stubs (old addresses kept working). | None needed. |

EXTERNAL, checked and fine: `/email/preferences` (unsubscribe link, via
`/api/email/unsubscribe`), `/landlord/[token]` (SMS to the landlord on a mandate),
`/safe/[token]` (safety share link to a friend), `/offline` (service worker fallback).

## Is it good: scores from source, not a signed-in walk

Each score is a heuristic read of the source, **not** a walk through the signed-in
product, and it is generous where the source cannot show the look. It rewards the
shared primitives (`ListGroup`, `Money`, `Sheet`, `State`, `PageHeader`,
`EmptyState`, `Row`, `BackControl`, `InnerNav` and kin), a loading state, an error
boundary or handled failure, a designed empty state, copy from the dictionary, and
metadata; it marks down placeholder screens, browser `confirm()`, and tables with no
scroll or stacking wrapper. Capped at 88: nothing reaches the section 0 bar on
source alone.

- 220 scored (4 stubs). Mean 79. 114 at 80 or more, 72 at 70 to 79, 32 at 60 to 69, 2 under 60.
- By area: `/agent` 86, `/host` 86, `/u` 84, `/settings` 82, `/admin` 75, `/profile` 75.
- Most common marks: no shared primitives (46, mostly legal, site and auth pages
  that use their own layouts), no empty state (46), tables with no wrapper (9, of
  which 5 in admin), `window.confirm` (4: the feed's delete, through `Feed.tsx`,
  against the DragToConfirm rule).
- Lowest: `/offline` 50, `/auth/callback` 59, `/profile/setup/agent` and `/owner` 63,
  the four public legal pages 63, `/guides` 63, `/r` 63, `/welcome` 63.
